questions.question: Explain the three-step procedure for applying the Master Theorem to a recurrence of the form $T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n)$. Your answer should mention what is compared and what final information must be reported.
questions.expected: A complete answer should: identify $a$, $b$, and $f(n)$; compute the threshold $n^{\log_b a}$; compare $f(n)$ with that threshold using the Master Theorem cases; then state both the case number and the asymptotic solution for $T(n)$. For simple-form recurrences $T(n)=aT(n/b)+\Theta(n^c)$, this is equivalent to comparing $c$ with $\log_b a$.

questions.question: Why does the general Master Theorem require a polynomial gap in cases $1$ and $3$? Explain using the example $f(n)=n^{\log_b a}/\log n$.
questions.expected: Cases $1$ and $3$ require $f(n)$ to be polynomially smaller or larger than $n^{\log_b a}$, meaning a factor of $n^\varepsilon$ for some $\varepsilon>0$. The function $f(n)=n^{\log_b a}/\log n$ is smaller only by a logarithmic factor, not a polynomial factor, so it falls into the gap where the standard Master Theorem cases do not apply.

questions.question: Solve the recurrence $T(n)=9T(n/3)+n^2$. State the Master Theorem case and the final asymptotic bound.
questions.expected: Here $a=9$, $b=3$, and $f(n)=n^2$. Since $n^{\log_3 9}=n^2$, this is case $2$. Therefore $T(n)=\Theta(n^2\log n)$.

questions.question: Solve the recurrence $T(n)=7T(n/2)+n^2$. State the Master Theorem case and the final asymptotic bound.
questions.expected: Here $a=7$, $b=2$, and $c=2$. Since $\log_2 7\approx 2.807$ and $2<\log_2 7$, this is case $1$. Therefore $T(n)=\Theta(n^{\log_2 7})$, approximately $\Theta(n^{2.807})$.

questions.question: Give pseudocode for a divide-and-conquer closest-pair algorithm on points in the plane. The expected running time should satisfy $T(n)=2T(n/2)+\Theta(n)$ after the initial sort.
questions.expected:
A correct sketch sorts once, recurses on left and right halves, and checks only the vertical strip around the split line.

```text
ClosestPair(points):
    Px = points sorted by x-coordinate
    Py = points sorted by y-coordinate
    return ClosestPairRec(Px, Py)

ClosestPairRec(Px, Py):
    n = length(Px)
    if n <= 3:
        return brute_force_closest_pair(Px)

    mid = n // 2
    x_mid = Px[mid].x
    Lx = Px[0:mid]
    Rx = Px[mid:n]
    Ly = [p in Py where p.x <= x_mid]
    Ry = [p in Py where p.x > x_mid]

    delta_left = ClosestPairRec(Lx, Ly)
    delta_right = ClosestPairRec(Rx, Ry)
    delta = min(delta_left, delta_right)

    strip = [p in Py where abs(p.x - x_mid) < delta.distance]
    best = delta
    for i from 0 to length(strip) - 1:
        for j from i + 1 to min(i + 7, length(strip) - 1):
            best = min(best, distance_pair(strip[i], strip[j]))
    return best
```

The initial sorting costs $\Theta(n\log n)$, and the recursive part has recurrence $T(n)=2T(n/2)+\Theta(n)$, so the total time is $\Theta(n\log n)$.

questions.question: Write pseudocode for Karatsuba multiplication of two $n$-bit integers $I$ and $J$. Your algorithm should use three recursive multiplications and should imply the recurrence $T(n)=3T(n/2)+\Theta(n)$.
questions.expected:
A correct sketch splits each number into high and low halves, computes three products, and combines them using shifts.

```text
Karatsuba(I, J, n):
    if n <= 1:
        return I * J

    m = ceil(n / 2)
    base = 2^m

    I_L = I mod base
    I_H = floor(I / base)
    J_L = J mod base
    J_H = floor(J / base)

    z0 = Karatsuba(I_L, J_L, m)
    z2 = Karatsuba(I_H, J_H, m)
    z1 = Karatsuba(I_L + I_H, J_L + J_H, m + 1)

    middle = z1 - z2 - z0
    return z2 * base^2 + middle * base + z0
```

The three recursive calls are on roughly half-size inputs, and splitting, addition, subtraction, and shifting cost $\Theta(n)$, so $T(n)=3T(n/2)+\Theta(n)=\Theta(n^{\log_2 3})$.
